messages:
maria: Quick follow-up from the postmortem — we need a concrete tiny playbook for phased rollouts that includes an automated containment window and a strict auto-rollback signature. TL;DR: owners, timers, and a clear metric set.
akash: +1. can we make the containment window configurable per-flag and per-route? some models tolerate longer convergence.
devon: We should also define what 'signature' means. My suggestion: combination of error-rate spike + tail latency + output-quality regression on a small eval set.
lee: Agree. For error-rate spike let's say >3x baseline in 5m and tail p99 > 2x baseline in same window triggers quarantine; quality regression >2% on the canary eval triggers auto-rollback.
maria: Sounds reasonable. Can we document this as fields in the flag gating config so infra can act automatically? Something like:

```
flag_gating:
  containment_window: 10m
  auto_rollback_signatures:
    - name: error_latency_combo
      error_rate_multiplier: 3.0
      p99_latency_multiplier: 2.0
    - name: quality_regress
      eval_set: "canary_prompt_set_v1"
      quality_drop_pct: 2.0
```

akash: That YAML looks good. We also need a fallback routing policy to pin traffic to a lower-capacity variant instead of full rollback for 10m to give time for human review.
devon: Yes — fallback should be pluggable: [pin-to-previous-model, redirect-region, reduce-sample-rate].
maria: Action items:
• maria — write the gating YAML spec and a short README (due: 3 business days)
• akash — implement the containment window timer + fallback routing hook in the runtime (due: 2 weeks)
• devon — add the quality-eval integration and baseline snapshots (due: 1 week)
• lee — owner of the auto-rollback playbook and runbook edits (due: 2 business days)

lee: I'll also make an automation that annotates the postmortem with the chosen gating config id so ops can see what was deployed during incident.
oncall-bot: NOTE: new playbook PRs should include a quick test harness run: `./scripts/run-quarantine-smoke.sh` — failures block merge.
akash: Small but important: add telemetry counters for 'quarantine-triggered', 'rollback-executed', and 'fallback-activated' so we can spot recurrence patterns.
maria: Good call. Let's add a recurring 30-day review in the runbook to look for patterns across incidents: owner rotates weekly for the review meeting.
devon: For rollout cadence, propose phases: 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with health checks between phases and a maximum time cap per-phase (default 60m).
lee: One more: include a manual 'hold' tag that prevents auto-promotion beyond current phase until a human approves; useful for high-risk models.
maria: I'll open the RFC and PRs today. I'll link infra tickets and a shared checklist. If nobody objects, I'll file tasks using the action items above.
akash: no objections from me. :thumbsup:
devon: fine by me. I'll start the eval hooks tomorrow.
lee: ack. I'll update the runbook and add the 30-day review calendar.
maria: thanks everyone — will post links once the RFC + PRs are up.
